age.evidence: All experiments were performed on 8- to 14-week-old male rats.

sex.evidence: All experiments were performed on 8- to 14-week-old male rats.

dosing.evidence: For all experiments, DMT·fumarate (2:1) was administered at 10 mg/kg via intraperitoneal injection using an injection volume of 1 mL/kg. (Acute single dose for NIL/EPM/FC/extinction assays; FST used a subchronic 3-dose regimen at 23.5, 6, 1 h before test.)

handling.evidence: Methods section does not mention any handling/habituation of animals by experimenters.

group_housing.evidence: Sprague-Dawley rats were obtained from Charles River Laboratories, were housed two per cage, and were given ad libitum access to food and water.

day_night_flipped.evidence: Lights in the vivarium were turned on at 07:00 hours and turned off at 19:00 hours. Studies were performed during the light-on phase, with experiments taking place between 08:00 and 18:00 hours.

enrichment_housing.evidence: Methods section does not mention home-cage enrichment.

assays.assay_description: 45-min open field test in 41.9 x 41.9 x 28.6 cm AccuScan Digiscan chamber (25-30 lux). Measures: total distance, thigmotaxis, number and time of rearings, number and time of stereotypies; recorded in 1-min bins.

application_type.evidence: DMT·fumarate (2:1) was administered at 10 mg/kg via intraperitoneal injection

setup_habituation.evidence: Animals were allowed to acclimate to the test room for 10 mins prior to being gently placed into the center of an AccuScan open field chamber (room acclimation, not apparatus habituation).

setup_restrain.evidence: allowed to freely explore the chamber for 45 mins

food_restriction.evidence: No food was present in the open field chamber during the 45-min test.

water_restriction.evidence: No water was present in the open field chamber during the 45-min test.

time_to_assay.evidence: Drug-naïve rats were administered either DMT or vehicle 1 hr before behavioral testing.

sample_size.evidence: Sample sizes not stated in available text.

outcomes.summary: DMT (10 mg/kg, 1 h pre-test) reduced exploratory behavior: shorter total distance, fewer and shorter rearings, and reduced time spent in stereotypies. Thigmotaxis and total stereotypy count were unaffected.
outcomes.evidence: DMT-treated animals displayed reduced exploratory behavior and traveled a significantly shorter total distance than vehicle-treated controls, but the drug did not affect thigmotaxis. Both the number of rearings and time spent rearing were significantly reduced by DMT.

B1_num_measures.evidence: total distance, thigmotaxis, number of rearings, time spent rearing, number of stereotypies, time spent in stereotypies

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Horizontal motion, rotations, and stereotypies (repetitive beam breaks) were recorded in 1-min intervals for the duration of the test

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No analysis of behavioural sequences/transitions reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: Rearing (number and time) is a natural exploratory behaviour directly measured.

B5_social.evidence: Animals tested alone in open field.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Open field locomotion does not require learning.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: AccuScan Digiscan beam-break system analyzed with Integra — position/beam-break only.

E3_bedding.evidence: Standard open field arena, no bedding mentioned.

E6_spatial.evidence: Single open field arena with virtual margin zone.

assays.assay_description: 5-min test on plus-shaped maze elevated 50 cm, 20-25 lux. Measures: % time in open arms, open-arm entries, total distance, average velocity, closed-arm entries. Tracked with EthoVision XT.

application_type.evidence: rats were administered DMT or vehicle 1 hr before being placed into the center of the maze

setup_habituation.evidence: No apparatus pre-exposure mentioned for EPM.

setup_restrain.evidence: allowed to explore freely for 5 min

food_restriction.evidence: No food in EPM apparatus during the test.

water_restriction.evidence: No water in EPM apparatus during the test.

time_to_assay.evidence: administered DMT or vehicle 1 hr before being placed into the center of the maze

sample_size.evidence: Closed arm entries: VEH n implied; sample sizes not explicitly stated in text.

outcomes.summary: DMT decreased % time in open arms and number of open arm entries (anxiogenic effect) without altering total distance, velocity, or closed-arm entries, indicating no locomotor confound.
outcomes.statistics: Closed arm entries: VEH = 9.375 ± 1.179; DMT = 8.556 ± 1.642; P = 0.6977, Student's t-test.
outcomes.evidence: DMT-treated animals spent a decreased percentage of time in the open arms of the maze and had a fewer number of open arm entries. The total distance traveled in the maze and the average velocity of the rodents were not statistically different between DMT-treated and vehicle-treated groups.

B1_num_measures.evidence: % time in open arms, open arm entries, total distance, average velocity, closed arm entries

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Reported as totals over the 5-min session.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: EthoVision XT (position tracking) — not behavioural classification.

E2_shelter.evidence: EPM closed arms are not scored as shelter per rubric.

E6_spatial.evidence: EPM scored as single open space per rubric.

D2_session_duration.evidence: allowed to explore freely for 5 min

assays.assay_description: Three-day cued+contextual fear conditioning in Med Associates chamber. Day 1: DMT/vehicle 1 h before conditioning (3.5 min baseline + 3 tone-shock pairings, 0.8 mA). Day 2: 10-min contextual test. Day 3: 2 min baseline + 8 tones in novel context for cued test. Measure: % freezing (Video Freeze software).

application_type.evidence: drug-naïve animals were administered either DMT or vehicle 1 hr prior to conditioning (via i.p. injection per Methods)

setup_restrain.evidence: Rats freely moving in conditioning chamber.

time_to_assay.evidence: drug-naïve animals were administered either DMT or vehicle 1 hr prior to conditioning

sample_size.evidence: Sample sizes not stated in available text.

outcomes.summary: DMT did not alter pre-shock freezing but acutely increased freezing immediately after the training shocks. Contextual (day 2) and cued (day 3) fear memory were indistinguishable between DMT- and vehicle-treated animals.
outcomes.evidence: Administration of DMT had no effect on initial freezing behavior prior to receiving foot shocks, however, it did significantly increase freezing immediately after the rodents received the training foot shocks ... DMT did not have a lasting impact on fear memory, as both contextual and cued fear memory, assessed in the days following conditioning, were indistinguishable between DMT- and vehicle-treated animals.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Pre-shock freezing, post-shock freezing, contextual freezing, cued freezing — all freezing measure across phases.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Med Associates Video Freeze — motion threshold detection, not behavioural classifier per rubric.

D1_continuity.evidence: Day 1 conditioning, Day 2 contextual test, Day 3 cued test.

D2_session_duration.evidence: Longest session = 10-min contextual test on Day 2.

D4_baseline.evidence: DMT had no effect on initial freezing behavior prior to receiving foot shocks (within-session pre-shock baseline recorded on Day 1 after drug; but Day 2/3 are post-acute recordings — see D5).

D5_followup.evidence: Contextual (day 2) and cued (day 3) tests assessed >=24 h after Day 1 DMT injection.

assays.assay_description: Animals fear-conditioned (no drug) on Day 1, rest Day 2, DMT/vehicle 1 h before extinction training on Day 3 (2 min baseline + 8 tones in novel context). Day 4 extinction recall in absence of drug. Measure: % freezing during tones.

application_type.evidence: animals were administered either DMT or vehicle 1 hr prior to extinction training (i.p.)

time_to_assay.evidence: animals were administered either DMT or vehicle 1 hr prior to extinction training

sample_size.evidence: Sample sizes not stated in available text.

outcomes.summary: DMT given before extinction training enhanced cued fear extinction: on Day 4 (drug-free recall), DMT-treated rats froze significantly less to the tones than vehicle-treated controls.
outcomes.evidence: Tone presentations caused the DMT-treated group to freeze significantly less than the control group, indicating that DMT administered prior to extinction training resulted in a stronger extinction memory.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Single freezing measure (% time freezing during tones).

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Reported as freezing during tone presentations.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Fear extinction is a learning/memory paradigm.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Med Associates Video Freeze — motion threshold.

E3_bedding.evidence: Smooth plastic floor insert in novel context.

D1_continuity.evidence: Day 1 conditioning + Day 3 extinction training + Day 4 recall.

D4_baseline.evidence: No pre-drug baseline of extinction freezing.

D5_followup.evidence: Day 4 extinction recall tested in absence of drug, ~24 h after DMT dose.

assays.assay_description: Strong foreground contextual conditioning (6 × 1.0 mA shocks) on Day 1, rest Day 2, DMT/vehicle 1 h before context re-exposure (10 min) on Days 3, 4, 5; Day 6 drug-free recall (10 min). Measure: % freezing over the 10-min session.

application_type.evidence: they were administered either DMT or vehicle 1 hr prior being placed in the fear conditioning context (i.p.)

time_to_assay.evidence: administered either DMT or vehicle 1 hr prior being placed in the fear conditioning context

sample_size.evidence: Sample sizes not stated in available text.

outcomes.summary: DMT given before each contextual extinction session did not significantly reduce freezing on the Day 6 drug-free recall versus vehicle; data showed a bimodal distribution suggesting responder/non-responder subgroups.
outcomes.statistics: Mann-Whitney test used due to bimodal distribution; not significant.
outcomes.evidence: The DMT-treated animals were not statistically different from the vehicle control group ... data from the contextual extinction experiment had a bimodal distribution, suggesting that there were responders and non-responders to contextual extinction training.

B1_num_measures.evidence: % time spent freezing over the 10-min session.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Contextual extinction is a learning/memory paradigm.

E3_bedding.evidence: Metal grated floor in conditioning context.

D1_continuity.evidence: Day 1 conditioning + Days 3, 4, 5 extinction + Day 6 recall.

D5_followup.evidence: Day 6 recall conducted in absence of drug, ~24 h after last DMT dose.

assays.assay_description: Plexiglas cylinder (80 cm tall × 20 cm diameter) filled with 30 cm water at 24 ± 1°C. Day 1: 15-min pre-test (drug-naïve). Day 2: 5-min test. Animals received 3 i.p. doses of DMT (10 mg/kg), ketamine (10 mg/kg), or vehicle at 23.5, 6, and 1 h before test. Measures: immobility, swimming, climbing counts (every 5 s).

application_type.evidence: DMT·fumarate (2:1) was administered at 10 mg/kg via intraperitoneal injection ... Each rat received three administrations of DMT, ketamine, or vehicle at 23.5, 6, and 1 hr before the test phase.

setup_habituation.evidence: Drug-naïve animals were subjected to a pre-test phase in which they were placed in the cylinder for 15 mins before being dried and returned to their home cage. (Conventional FST pre-test functions as apparatus pre-exposure.)

setup_restrain.evidence: Rats freely swimming in cylinder (no physical restraint device).

water_restriction.evidence: No drinking water access during the swim test.

time_to_assay.evidence: Each rat received three administrations of DMT, ketamine, or vehicle at 23.5, 6, and 1 hr before the test phase.

sample_size.evidence: Sample sizes not stated in available text.

outcomes.summary: DMT significantly reduced immobility and increased swimming counts compared with vehicle, with no change in climbing. Effects were indistinguishable from ketamine, indicating antidepressant-like activity.
outcomes.statistics: One-way ANOVA with Tukey post-hoc test.
outcomes.evidence: DMT significantly decreased the amount of time the rodents spent immobile and increased the amount of time they spent swimming. There was no significant difference in climbing behavior between DMT- and vehicle-treated animals ... the effects of DMT in the FST were indistinguishable from those of the fast-acting antidepressant ketamine.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Behaviour quantified as total counts over the 5-min test.

B4_ethological.evidence: FST behaviours are not natural ethological behaviours per rubric.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Each video was scored ... by a trained observer.

E7_social_context.evidence: Fresh water used for each rat; tested individually.

D2_session_duration.evidence: pre-test phase in which they were placed in the cylinder for 15 mins

D3_recording_days.evidence: Pre-test day + test day (24 h later).

D4_baseline.evidence: Drug-naïve pre-test phase recorded on Day 1 before any drug administration.

D5_followup.evidence: Test conducted 1 h after last dose; no ≥24 h post-acute recording.

judge_notes: Split candidates' combined 'Fear Conditioning (including extinction)' into three separate assays — Fear Conditioning, Cued Fear Extinction, Contextual Fear Extinction — because the paper runs them as three distinct experiments on different cohorts with different protocols (drug given at conditioning vs. at extinction; cued vs. contextual extinction recall).
B4 (ethological) for NIL scored 1 because rearing — a natural exploratory act — is explicitly quantified as a discrete behaviour (number and time), beyond simple locomotion.

Setup_habituation for FST scored 'yes' because the 15-min Day 1 pre-test functions as standard apparatus pre-exposure (data recorded but the conventional FST design uses it as habituation to the swim apparatus).
Dosing schedule labeled 'acute' overall since most assays used a single dose; FST 3-dose subchronic regimen is noted in evidence rather than creating a separate dosing entry.
FST D4 (baseline) scored 'yes' because the Day 1 pre-test is recorded drug-naïve in the same apparatus before any DMT administration.
